audit_notes: Parameters positive and consistent: s=80 um > h=40 um (h/s=0.5). u_tau = sqrt(50/1025)=0.221 m/s, l_nu = 1.19e-6/0.221 = 5.4 um -> s+ = 14.8 (inside the 10-20 drag-reducing window), h+ = 7.4. Protrusion-height difference 4.5 um = 0.056 s is consistent with Luchini et al. (1991) values for trapezoidal/blade riblets (0.03-0.08 s) -> Delta h+ = 0.83, Delta U+ ~ 0.83 -> DR ~ 2*0.83/35 = 4.7%. The model is a laminar-equivalent wall layer of thickness 95 um (17.5 viscous units, chosen so that b/(delta+b) = 2 b+/U_b+), with fixed edge velocity 3.9 m/s. Analytical solution u = U_d (b/delta + y)/(1 + b/delta), wall shear tau = mu U_d /(delta+b); gain = b/(delta+b) = 4.5%. Simulation coefficient: the pipeline's riblet formula 0.2 s (1-exp(-2h/s)) = 0.2*80e-6*0.632 = 10.1 um; this generic formula gives roughly twice the Luchini protrusion difference and would overstate DR; the equations use effective_protrusion_difference (4.5 um), so the coefficient is informational. Structural: PDMS crests E=1 MPa under 50 Pa shear: tip deflection of a 40 um tall, ~5 um thick crest under distributed shear ~ tau*h^4/(E*t^3)*(order 1.5) ~ 50*2.56e-18/(1e6*1.25e-16)*1.5 = 1 um -> small flexing, consistent with the claim of modest compliance; no collapse. Durability concern (not a physical safety issue): soft PDMS riblets abrade under cleaning; fouling in grooves is the dominant risk. Baseline: smooth clean FR wall = zero protrusion difference.

performance_gain.label: Skin-friction reduction vs smooth FR hull

baseline_description: Clean hydraulically smooth silicone foul-release coating (no riblets)
